newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Buying opportunity awaits dlr bulls in '97.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Buying opportunity awaits dlr bulls in '97.

text.p: The U.S. dollar will likely bounce back after New Year as its across-the-board pullback provides a buying opportunity for key players away from the market on the last day of 1996, analysts said on Tuesday.
In thin late Tuesday trading, the dollar was quoted at 116.03/13 yen versus 116.12/17 late Monday, at 1.5395/05 marks vs 1.5545/55, and at 1.3395/05 Swiss francs vs 1.3482/92.
Analysts said with 115.20-yen support in no danger of falling, the dollar is likely to soon retest resistance at 116.20 -- the 45-month high versus the yen set on Friday and revisited on Friday.

Currency strategist David Durrant at I.D.E.A. said the sharp pullback of the dollar against the European currencies in the cash market appeared driven by limited selling in the futures market early in Tuesday's session.
"Markets are always susceptible to a large move in thin trade," said Durrant who noted the dollar selloff "created a buying opportunity or allowed to cover at low levels."
"It was an opportunity more than a real move," added Durrant who pointed out that, whatever the motivation was, the player who pushed dollar futures lower "got the desired effect from this."
Technicians said if the dollar should be able to hold above 1.5350-mark support and march against a series of resistance levels in the 1.55- to 1.56-mark area.
On dollar/yen, analysts said a six-day rising trendline was tested at 115.70 but held -- keeping alive prospects for another bull run at 116.20, and then 117.30.

On dollar/Swiss, the downside is limited with support at 1.3340 apparently in no imminent danger. The first resistance at 1.3450 Swiss francs appears within reach, which would open the scope for a run at 1.3515, technicians also said.
As for cable, after a stunning run, it looks overbought.
"We are seeing levels you would not normally see," said Durrant. "If you are a dollar bull, you're provided with a definitive opportunity."
Sterling was quoted late Tuesday at $1.7120/30 vs $1.6900/10 late Monday.
Mark/yen may hold the key to the dollar's next trend.

Fresh yen weakness could send the German currency soaring and hammer dollar/mark in the process. At 75.25/35, mark/yen is giving no clear signal of pushing to 75.90 resistance or retreating below key support at 74.40.
